summary.whatChanges: Changes Zod's object type inference so index-signature shapes use a mapped type (`{ [k in string]: ... }`) instead of `Record<string, ...>`, which lets self-referential recursive object schema type aliases resolve. Adds type-level and runtime tests in both the classic and mini test suites.
behaviorChanges: Recursive type aliases like `type F = z.ZodObject<{ [k: string]: F }>` now infer concrete input/output types instead of failing to resolve
z.input/z.output for schemas with string index-signature shapes resolve through a mapped type, preserving distinct input vs output types in recursive unions
Key type of inferred indexed objects remains `string` (asserted by new tests)
Same fix applies to zod/mini object inference
risks: Mapped type vs Record may subtly alter inferred type display or assignability in downstream code, affecting compile results for existing users
Change is type-level only; no runtime validation behavior is altered, so any runtime expectation from the new tests relies on existing behavior
Deeply recursive aliases could still hit TypeScript recursion/instantiation depth limits not covered by the added tests
